headline: Oil extended its rise after Thursday's close — Brent printed near $83.59 in evening trading versus its $82.49 settle — with the Strait of Hormuz announcement still pending and the July jobs report due before Friday's open.
stance: Little has changed since the evening brief, and that is the story: oil is still climbing after hours — Brent near $83.59 in evening trading against Thursday's $82.49 settle — while the promised Iran–Oman announcement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz has not come. With private payrolls at their weakest in six months, Friday morning's July jobs report (consensus near 85,000) remains the print that decides whether the roughly 62% market-implied odds of a September hike hold.

news.head: Oil keeps climbing after the close
news.body: Brent printed near $83.59 in Thursday evening trading, above its $82.49 Thursday settle (up 3.8% on the day); the shipping-route agreement Iran said it reached with Oman has still not been jointly announced, and the strait remains blockaded.

news.head: Gold eases off its evening highs
news.body: Gold printed near $4,292 in Thursday evening trading after reaching about $4,342 earlier in the evening — still above the levels that prevailed for most of July.

news.head: Labor week closes soft ahead of the jobs report
news.body: The week's tally into Friday: 44,000 private-sector jobs added in July (weakest in six months), weekly claims historically low at 199,000, and announced July job cuts at a two-year low — hiring is slowing while firing stays scarce.

news.head: Software strength held through the evening
news.body: Atlassian (about +33%), Doximity (about +66%), Twilio and Cloudflare (about +16% each) surged in Thursday's after-market on earnings — Friday's opening prints will show how much sticks.

implications: An oil market rising into a pending peace announcement is pricing announcement risk, not resolution: if the Iran–Oman route deal lands, the evening's gains are the first thing at risk; if it slips, Brent's move from $79.40 (Wednesday's close) to the mid-$83s becomes the new inflation input for the Fed debate.

Friday's July jobs report remains binary for the front end: futures pricing implies roughly 62% odds of a quarter-point September hike, and this week's soft private-sector data has not moved it — the official print will.

Positioning: Unchanged from this morning's read and still the freshest extreme: speculators' Treasury longs sit at the 97th percentile of the last three years in 5-year futures and the 87th in 2-year (new this week) — a contrarian warning for those notes if payrolls print hot.

watch.head: July jobs report (8:30am-hour Friday, before the open)
watch.body: Consensus near 85,000 jobs with unemployment expected at 4.2%–4.3%, against June's 57,000; the decisive print of the week after the 44,000 private-payrolls miss.

watch.head: The Hormuz announcement window
watch.body: Iran said a joint announcement with Oman on a reopened shipping route was imminent; each hour it slips, oil holds its evening gains — Brent near $83.59 late Thursday.

watch.head: Friday opening prints for Thursday's after-hours movers
watch.body: Atlassian, Doximity, Twilio and Cloudflare all carried double-digit after-market gains into the evening; whether they hold at the open is the cleanest read on enterprise-software demand.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The single change since the evening brief: oil kept rising after the close — Brent near $83.59 in Thursday evening trading versus its $82.49 settle, with the Iran–Oman shipping-route announcement for the Strait of Hormuz still not delivered and the strait still blockaded.

Rates enter the jobs print with the 10-year at 4.67% (Thursday's close, up from 4.63% Wednesday) and the 2-year at 4.18% (Wednesday's close); futures pricing implies roughly 62% odds of a quarter-point September hike.
Friday's July jobs report: consensus near 85,000 (range roughly 80,000–100,000), unemployment expected at 4.2%–4.3%, against June's 57,000 — after a week of soft private-sector hiring data.
Gold printed near $4,292 in Thursday evening trading, easing from about $4,342 earlier in the evening; the 10-year real (inflation-adjusted) yield closed Wednesday at 2.41%.
sections.positioning: Unchanged from this morning and still the freshest read: speculators are extended long the belly of the Treasury curve — 5-year futures at the 97th percentile of the last three years and 2-year at the 87th, both new this week. The bond market is leaning hard toward a weak-jobs, rate-relief outcome; a hot payrolls print is the risk to that bet.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Thursday's cash closes stand: S&P 500 down 0.2% at 7,709.96, Dow down 0.9% at 53,885.10 a day after its record close, Nasdaq down 0.1% at 26,348.35 — with the S&P 500 still up about 3.7% from its July 30 close.
The after-market earnings winners held into the evening — Atlassian about +33%, Doximity about +66%, Twilio and Cloudflare about +16% each — early-evening indications, not Friday opening prints.

Volatility remains quiet into the jobs print: the VIX sat near 15.9 Thursday evening (15.81 at Wednesday's close), and tail-risk pricing (133 at Wednesday's close, versus about 140 a week earlier) has eased rather than built.
sections.positioning: Standing backdrop, not new: speculators have held almost no bullish bets in Russell 2000 futures for 14 straight weeks — a three-year low that acts as a contrarian floor under small caps.

single_name.note: (Taiwan Semiconductor — the foundry at the center of the AI build-out) - company insiders have been buying, with a fresh purchase filing this week; the shares trade above their 200-day trend line and the setup's dark-pool and options signals are live.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Nothing new after hours — credit closed the day calm: the high-yield-over-investment-grade spread at 273 basis points and investment-grade spreads at 78 basis points (both Tuesday's close), narrower than late July.

Funding markets remain quiet: the key bank-funding spreads closed Wednesday at about 1 basis point; the overnight reverse-repo facility is essentially empty at $1.6 billion (Wednesday), with bank reserves at $2,984.6 billion (July 29).
The evening's oil move leans directly on the bond market's calm inflation view: the 10-year breakeven inflation rate closed Wednesday at 2.22% — every additional dollar on Brent tests it.
